program: Counseling, legal assistance, shelter and economic empowerment for survivors

acceptance.evidence: docs/geography-discovery/nyc-sanctuary-independent-20261005.md: original-source challenge, independent signed welfare arithmetic and exact historical-model preservation accepted. Conditional reference, not empirical expected value or gift guarantee.

priceScope: Conditional marginal unrestricted-gift judgment reference; 10 healthy-year equivalents combining health and signed net-consumption welfare

what: Sanctuary provides counseling and crisis support to survivors of gender violence and their children.
Its lawyers help clients with protection, immigration, housing, public benefits and family matters.
It also provides shelter, career training, job placement and practical financial support.
strengths: An integrated service portfolio addresses safety, mental health and financial barriers.
Original financial statements distinguish donated legal services from paid resources.
Career support includes childcare access, transportation and other practical assistance.
reservations: The $207.1M reference per 10 healthy-year equivalents depends on unmeasured health and financial effects.
Service reach, placements and salaries do not establish additional benefit beyond other providers.
Marginal expansion, survivor-controlled resources, harms and client overlap remain unknown.

sections.what: Sanctuary for Families, Inc., EIN 13-3193119, operates with New Beginnings Housing Development Fund Corporation in the consolidated portfolio. We assess unrestricted support across its services. Training, internships and placement may improve economic resources; legal work may secure benefits, housing and support. [EEP](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/our-approach/client-services/economic-empowerment-services/) [Legal services](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/our-approach/client-services/legal-services/)
sections.monitoring: FY24–25 reports 9,230 adults and children served, more than 2,600 clinical/crisis clients, more than 7,000 legal clients, 428 shelter residents and more than 450 broad economic-support clients. These are people, not sessions; cross-program uniqueness and therapy completion are undisclosed, so do not sum them. The impact page says 65% find work within one year; EEP reports $41k average salaries without a current annual cohort or comparison group. Neither establishes causal earnings or survivor-controlled net consumption. Feedback and progress forms support monitoring. Needed: deduplicated adults/households, all-entrant follow-up, exposure, retention, baseline/comparison consumption, taxes, benefit withdrawal, work costs and resource control. [Annual report](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Sanctuary-for-Families-Annual-Report-FY24-25.pdf) [Impact](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/impact/impact-and-results/) [Evaluation](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/impact/evaluation/)
sections.qualitative: PATH randomized normal advocacy against advocacy plus eight psychological sessions and two follow-ups in 260 UK women; 64% had twelve-month follow-up. Depression and distress improved, but physical health and further abuse did not differ; missing-data imputation reduced effects. This supports a mental-health mechanism, not Sanctuary's utility, response or injury prevention. The new reference removes uncalibrated shelter-injury credit and halves the prior response (.10 to .05), utility (.08 to .04) and duration (one year to half a year). These choices test mixed crisis/referral/therapy exposure, transfer and persistence uncertainty; they are judgments, not fitted trial coefficients. Shelter can still provide safety and housing value. Retaliation, stress and retraumatization are possible harms; adverse-event imbalance does not prove a causal harm rate. [PATH](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0205485)
sections.cost: Conditional reference: $207,106,666 per 10 NYC-MSA healthy-year equivalents, separating health QALYs from signed independent consumption welfare. This is not an empirical expected value. Annual average non-donated spending is about $3,677 per reported client, or 0.000272 reported client-years of reach per budget dollar; additional reach from an actual gift is unknown. The assumed half-capacity expansion produces 0.000001915 additional clinical responders per dollar. Financial pathways use distinct adult resource recipients, not visits, gross wages or household multipliers. Judgment priors: 67.5 workforce adults (15% of a 450-person broad-support anchor) and 200 disjoint legal/benefits adults; $20,000 baseline consumption; net gains $1,500/$1,000; .25 additional-resource shares; one finite year and one/.5-year delays. A 3% time discount plus .005 ordinary mortality attrition applies; no survival benefit or ordinary extra survivor income is credited. Half positive financial welfare remains after health overlap; negative costs receive full weight across all 450 exposed workforce adults and 200 legal adults without a success multiplier. Positive, negative, clinical-null, neutral, zero-expansion and unknown cases are explicit. The old $34,644,592.51237719 alpha health-only price rises because clinical assumptions shrink and injury credit is removed, partly offset by conditional financial welfare; the full original model remains diagnostic. Full donated-resource burden gives $626,309,186 per 10 combined healthy-year equivalents with unchanged annual outcomes and capacity; donated labor/goods are an economic resource cost, not the gift's marginal cash requirement.
sections.funding: FY25 operating expense $102,237,655 plus $387,934 donor event benefits gives $102,625,589 gross; removing $68,528,009 donated legal services and $161,556 goods gives $33,936,024 non-donated accrual cost. FY24 comparable cost is $31,917,251. All programs, overhead and event costs remain in scope; this is not cash outflow. The 990 reports $33,654,637: Schedule D subtracts pro bono services and $55,009 indirect fundraising from operating expense. Annual-summary $33,539,090 is $9,000 below comparable net non-donated operating expense; this residual remains unreconciled. Only two comparable original years are verified, so no three-year average is claimed. Public, fee and volunteer support stay baseline; no gift-funded expansion bottleneck is documented. The official donation route is live. [Audit](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Sanctuary-for-Families-FY25-Audit.pdf) [990](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Sanctuary-for-Families-990-FY25.pdf) [Donate](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/support-us/ways-to-donate/)

model.costScope: Full consolidated non-donated gross accrual cost C=$33,936,024. D=1 is arithmetic normalization, not a gift suggestion. b maps annual-recipient output to conditional marginal output; actual gift expansion unknown. Existing pro bono labor remains baseline. The reference is cash-like non-donated accrual, not cash flow. Full-resource sensitivity uses $102,625,589 including donated-resource valuation with identical annual outcomes and capacity assumptions.
model.geographicAttribution: .95 NYC MSA share based on local operations is a judgment, not measured residence. Half-share scenario tests leakage; policy benefits unpriced.
model.formula: Health=D/C*b*N*r*u*exp(-k*lag)*(1-exp(-k*T))/k; k=ln(1+d)-ln(1-m). Income=.5*people*discounted receipt-years*ln(1+net gain/baseline consumption)*causalShare*editionShare*independentShare; people=D/C*b*N. Income effective discount=(1+.03)/(1-.005)-1 includes common-alive attrition. .5 is the repository $50k/$100k welfare conversion. Health fields are health-only. Price10=10*D/(editionHealth+signedIncomeEquivalent) if total positive and known.
model.counterfactual: Existing public services, other workforce/clinical providers, legal aid, benefits and self-found jobs continue. Positive causalShare is an additional-resource fraction, not placement success. b is donor expansion separately. Negative scenarios charge exposed cohort costs with causalShare1.
model.attribution: Legal/benefits adults exclude workforce adults; no child or household multiplier. Positive financial independentShare.5 removes possible mental-health overlap; negative burdens retain1. No new shelter-injury or legal-to-health credit.
model.uncertainty: Explicit conditional judgment reference, not empirical expected value. Effects, consumption baseline, resource control, donor capacity and geography lack calibrated data; signed adverse, unknown and null cases remain.
model.nativeOutcomes: Reported annual people, additional clinical responders and distinct adults with retained consumption changes; gross wages, visits, jobs and case wins are not automatic QALYs.

sensitivity.assumptions: Benefit withdrawal, costs or lost resources outweigh gains; financial burdens persist when clinical effect is zero.

sensitivity.label: Stronger positive conditional expansion
sensitivity.assumptions: All stronger parameters are judgments, not measured forecasts.

sensitivity.label: Low expansion and short benefits
sensitivity.assumptions: Small effects and capacity with fixed whole-recipient cost.

sensitivity.label: No donor additionality
sensitivity.assumptions: Gift entirely substitutes for other funding; no new services or financial effect.

sensitivity.label: Adverse health and financial effects
sensitivity.assumptions: Stress/retaliation/retraumatization modeled as .001 QALY per annual clinical client plus net financial burdens; magnitude entirely hypothetical.

sensitivity.label: Health and income remain unknown
sensitivity.assumptions: No calibrated recipient causal-health utility, net resources or marginal expansion data: combined price is not identified.

sensitivity.label: Reference health, unknown signed income
sensitivity.assumptions: Conditional health retained; unknown financial welfare blocks combined price.

sensitivity.label: All financial welfare overlaps health
sensitivity.assumptions: No independent income-equivalent credit; health remains.

sensitivity.label: Positive health, negative net consumption
sensitivity.assumptions: Independent signed financial burdens reduce total despite positive clinical benefit.

sensitivity.label: Full donated-resource burden
sensitivity.assumptions: Same annual outcomes, causal/resource assumptions and capacity b as reference; cost denominator includes donated legal labor and goods, plus event benefits. Total-resource burden sensitivity, not actual marginal cash requirement.

missingInputs: Actual marginal expansion from unrestricted gifts
Deduplicated clinical exposure/completion, causal utility/duration and adverse events
Current workforce cohort net resources including taxes/benefits/work costs/control
Distinct legal/benefits adults, controlled consumption baseline and alternative-provider effects
Overlap, household allocation, residence and finite retention

incomeDecomposition.basis: Hypothetical judgment; not measured wage arithmetic
incomeDecomposition.negative: All450 broad-support adults are exposed in workforce-cost stress tests; no placement/causal-success dilution. Net losses -1500/-1000 at full causal/independent weight. Positive .25 resource attribution remains separate from assumed number exposed.
incomeDecomposition.baseline: $20k adult controlled annual consumption includes earnings, transfers and in-kind support; not zero earnings. No redistribution credited merely because survivor status changes.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: $1000 unrestricted gift scaled by all-recipient non-donated accrual cost including all support/event costs; current donated legal labor is baseline. Not social cost-effectiveness.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: g=.95 prior for service beneficiaries within NYC MSA, not measured residence allocation. National precedent benefits unpriced; sensitivity .5–1.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: For pathway j: k=ln(1+d)-ln(1-m_j); F_j=exp(-k*lag_j)*(1-exp(-k*T_j))/k (T if k=0). Qall=(D/C)*b*sum(N_j*r_j*u_j*F_j*o_j)-h; Qedition=(D/C)*b*sum(N_j*r_j*u_j*F_j*o_j*g_j)-h*gH. Price10=10*D/Qedition if positive. For uniformly timed injury events over W years multiply F by (1-exp(-k*W))/(k*W). The full episode T follows each event, so horizon is lag+W+T.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Public survivor services, existing clinicians and pro-bono support continue. r counts extra response or absolute injury probability reduction. No full volunteer network credit.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: b=.5 marginal output elasticity is a prior. Physical injury excludes mental-health sequelae and uses .75 residual-overlap factor. No restricted clinical allocation assumed.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Very weak. Clinical transfer, gift additionality and injury effects dominate. Zero or negative net health remains plausible.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Additional clinical responders and physical injury episodes prevented; not summed service contacts or legal wins.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Half average output per dollar is marginal; unmeasured substitution.

inputs.name: d
inputs.rationale: Sensitivity 0–5%.

inputs.name: h
inputs.rationale: Other net health zero provisionally; adverse scenario explicit.

inputs.name: gH
inputs.rationale: Local-service prior.
